personas.title: The Planner
personas.tagline: You like your money to have a job description.
personas.text: You decide before the month starts instead of during it. That is the strongest habit in this whole project - just leave a little room for surprises so one bad day does not break the whole plan.
tips: Keep a small unlabelled buffer line in your budget so surprises do not break it.
Review once a week, not every day - planning should not turn into worrying.
Add your savings transfer as the first line, not the last one left over.

personas.title: The Saver
personas.tagline: Watching the balance go up is your favourite reward.
personas.text: You protect your future money first, which puts you ahead of most students. The risk is the opposite one: saving so tightly that you never enjoy the month, then splurging all at once.
tips: Give the wants slice a name - a guilt-free treat is easier to stick to.
Name every goal with an amount and a date, otherwise saving drifts.
Hold one week of expenses as a buffer before chasing bigger targets.

personas.title: The Spender
personas.tagline: Money is for living, and you prove it often.
personas.text: You spend on moments and feelings, which is not a crime - but unplanned spending is what quietly empties a student budget. A few simple speed bumps change everything without killing the fun.
tips: Use the 48 hour rule: wait two days, then buy it guilt-free if you still want it.
Set a hard cap for food and fun at the start of the month, then stop when it hits.
Move a fixed amount to savings the day money arrives, before spending starts.

personas.title: The Balancer
personas.tagline: Save a little, live a little, regret nothing.
personas.text: You naturally sit between saving and spending, which keeps you consistent over long stretches. Your blind spot is the small drift - lots of near-neutral decisions that never get reviewed.
tips: Use 50-30-20 as your baseline so balance stays a choice, not an accident.
Do a ten minute money check-in each week to catch slow drift early.
Raise your savings share by one percent at a time instead of all at once.

questions.text: It is mid-month and your balance dropped faster than you expected. First move?

options.text: Open my tracker and find the category that broke
Cancel the rest of the month's fun spending
Shrug it off - next month will reset anyway
Trim a little everywhere but keep my plans

questions.text: You get an unexpected Rs 5,000 today. What happens first?

options.text: Straight into savings - future me says thanks
Add it to this month's plan and update the categories
Treat myself, it is bonus money
Split it - save half, enjoy half

questions.text: How do you usually track what you spend?

options.text: Same day, every entry written down
I do not track - I just watch the balance drop
Only transfers into my savings count
Rough mental math with a glance each week

questions.text: A friend suggests an expensive plan this weekend. Your move?

options.text: Check my wants budget, then decide
I go - experiences beat the price tag
I decline and move the money to my goal
I go, but pick a cheaper version of the plan

questions.text: A sale lands on something you have wanted for months. What now?

options.text: Buy it now - discounts do not wait
Wait two days and check my goal progress
Check whether it fits this month's plan and caps
Buy a cheaper alternative instead

questions.text: How often do you actually look at your savings goals?

options.text: Once a week, at the same time
Whenever I add money to them
Rarely - I forget they exist
About once a month, near month end
